approvalRequirements: Be a Verdigris Valley Electric Cooperative member with the equipment installed at an eligible service location.
Purchase new equipment currently listed by VVEC and meet the applicable ENERGY STAR, efficiency, system-configuration, and replacement requirements.
Use a certified dealer where required and obtain the applicable AHRI certificate, Manual J calculation, invoice, receipt, or other measure-specific documentation.
Submit the completed rebate form within 90 days of purchase.
Allow VVEC to conduct on-site verification of the new unit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: VVEC's current rebates use published customer, equipment, documentation, timing, and verification criteria rather than competitive selection. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid, but the current page does not support the legacy window or electric-vehicle-charger mappings.
reviews.evidenceText: VVEC currently lists heat-pump water heaters, smart thermostats, ground-source heat pumps, dual-fuel air-source heat pumps, and mini-splits. Forms are due within 90 days, used equipment is excluded, and on-site verification may occur.

approvalRequirements: Be a Vermont Electric Cooperative member eligible to receive a bill credit.
Purchase a new or used electric forklift for a new application or as a direct replacement for a fossil-fuel-powered forklift.
Complete the current online electric-forklift bill-credit form and provide the requested member, equipment, purchase, and replacement information.
Permit VEC to validate the transaction and member account before applying the credit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: VEC publishes a fixed bill credit with objective member, equipment, and purchase conditions. A documented qualifying forklift purchase is likely to receive the credit after routine review.
reviews.evidenceText: VEC currently offers a bill credit for new or used electric forklifts used in new applications or directly replacing fossil-fuel forklifts and directs members to an online claim form.

approvalRequirements: Be a Vermont Electric Cooperative member eligible to receive a bill credit.
Purchase or lease a qualifying new or used all-electric or plug-in hybrid electric vehicle.
Submit the current online form with the requested member, vehicle, purchase or lease, and registration documentation.
Provide current income documentation when seeking the additional income-qualified incentive.
Pass VEC's account and transaction validation before the bill credit is posted.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current vehicle credit is a published, noncompetitive member benefit. A qualifying vehicle transaction with complete documentation is likely to receive the stated credit, although the separate EV-charger measure mapped to this record belongs under VEC's charging-equipment offering.
reviews.evidenceText: VEC currently provides one-time bill credits for qualifying new or used all-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, whether purchased or leased, with an additional income-qualified amount.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible VEC member for a residential Level 2 charger, or an eligible business or public entity for a public charging-station credit.
Use qualifying Level 2 equipment or install an eligible publicly available Level 2 or Level 3 station.
For a no-cost or separately purchased residential charger, satisfy the applicable communications-platform, charging-schedule, and Beat the Peak participation terms.
For a public station, keep the charger publicly available and operational under the current program rules.
Submit the applicable online request or bill-credit form and provide the required account, charger, purchase, installation, and operating information.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: VEC's current charging offers have defined member, equipment, enrollment, scheduling, and public-access rules rather than competitive selection. A compliant applicant is likely to receive the charger or bill credit after review.
reviews.evidenceText: VEC currently offers no-cost managed Level 2 chargers, a credit for member-purchased Level 2 chargers meeting scheduling or communications terms, and per-connection credits for eligible public Level 2 or Level 3 stations.

approvalRequirements: Be a VEC member with a qualifying heat-pump installation at an eligible home or business.
Meet the current Efficiency Vermont technical, installer, equipment, and application requirements for the selected system.
Apply through Efficiency Vermont for the coordinated incentive on larger centrally ducted, ground-source, or air-to-water systems.
Submit VEC's online form when seeking the possible thermal-efficiency adder.
Provide installation and equipment documentation and pass any required partner or utility verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The legacy VEC bill-credit listing no longer describes a broad direct heat-pump credit. Most current support is administered through Efficiency Vermont, while VEC may provide only a limited thermal-efficiency adder, so an award depends on the specific system and partner-program qualification.
reviews.evidenceText: VEC states that heat-pump incentives are generally available through Efficiency Vermont and that no direct VEC incentive is available other than a possible thermal-efficiency adder; larger systems use a coordinated partner credit.

approvalRequirements: Be a Vermont Electric Cooperative member eligible for a bill credit.
Purchase an installed, nonportable induction cooktop on or after the current eligibility date.
Complete the online induction-cooktop credit form with the requested account, purchase, product, and installation information.
Permit VEC to validate the member account and qualifying purchase before applying the credit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: VEC publishes a fixed incentive with objective member, product, installation, and purchase-date requirements. A complete qualifying claim is likely to receive the bill credit.
reviews.evidenceText: VEC currently offers an incentive for installed induction cooktops purchased on or after September 1, 2022; portable units are excluded and members apply through an online form.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Vermont Gas Systems residential customer or property owner in the current service area.
Complete the required home evaluation and develop an eligible weatherization plan, with any heat-pump work included through the applicable financing option.
Use a qualified Building Performance Institute contractor and achieve the required air-leakage reduction for weatherization work.
Submit the financing application and project documentation and pass Green Mountain Credit Union credit underwriting or the applicable on-bill payment-history review.
Receive approval before relying on financing, complete the authorized project within the program period, and provide final installation and cost documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program has a defined project pathway, but financing is not automatic. Approval depends on weatherization eligibility, contractor and savings requirements, borrower credit or payment history, and final project review.
reviews.evidenceText: Vermont Gas describes home evaluation, qualified-contractor weatherization, project-plan review, and financing through a credit-union loan or eligible on-bill pathway, with borrower and project approval required before funding.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Vermont Gas Systems residential customer at the installation address.
Select equipment or weatherization work currently offered by Vermont Gas and meet the applicable fuel, efficiency, replacement, installation, and income requirements.
Use a licensed natural-gas contractor for qualifying gas equipment and a qualified weatherization contractor for envelope work.
Obtain the instant incentive through the participating contractor or distributor, or complete the required home-evaluation and weatherization application pathway.
Retain invoices, photographs, product records, and other substantiation and allow post-installation verification or inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current equipment rebates and weatherization support use published technical and documentation rules rather than competitive selection. A qualifying transaction is likely to receive the benefit, but the legacy generic waste-heat-recovery mapping is broader than the current drain-water heat-recovery offer.
reviews.evidenceText: Vermont Gas currently provides instant rebates for listed natural-gas equipment and controls and a separate evaluated weatherization pathway, with licensed contractors, current specifications, records, and possible verification.

approvalRequirements: No new Replace Your Ride application can be approved because Vermont reported that program funds were exhausted and the program closed in October 2024.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Vermont's current official reporting says Replace Your Ride exhausted its funding and closed, with no subsequent appropriation supporting a new application pathway. A new award is therefore rare unless the state creates and funds a future round.
reviews.evidenceText: Vermont's January 2026 legislative report states that Replace Your Ride exhausted its funds and closed in October 2024. A later official retrospective says the state clean-transportation incentive programs ended without additional funding.

approvalRequirements: Identify a currently open Volkswagen-settlement project category and the state agency or program sponsor administering that category.
Meet the sponsor-specific applicant, vehicle or equipment, site, scrappage or replacement, charging-infrastructure, eligible-cost, and cost-share requirements.
Submit the sponsor's complete application or proposal with the required technical, ownership, budget, environmental, and supporting documentation.
Receive the applicable administrative or competitive selection and execute the project or reimbursement agreement before undertaking restricted work.
Complete procurement, installation or vehicle replacement, reporting, inspection, scrappage, and reimbursement documentation required by the selected project.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: New York's Volkswagen settlement page is an umbrella for multiple sponsor programs with different technologies and statuses, including open, awarded, completed, and closed activities. Without a specific current subprogram and applicant, present award likelihood cannot be determined.
reviews.evidenceText: The current DEC page directs applicants to separate sponsor programs for diesel replacement and charging infrastructure. Each has its own eligibility, application, selection, agreement, and reimbursement process, and several listed rounds are no longer open.

approvalRequirements: No current Missouri application can be approved under this PowerMoves record because Wabash Valley Power Alliance's current member-cooperative territory is in Indiana and Illinois.
Any project evaluated under the active PowerMoves program must first be matched to a current participating member-cooperative account in the supported territory.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current official WVPA materials identify member distribution cooperatives in Indiana and Illinois, not Missouri. The legacy Missouri record therefore has no verified current award pathway.
reviews.evidenceText: PowerMoves' 2026 business program serves nonresidential customers of participating WVPA member cooperatives. Current WVPA materials describe a 21-member Indiana-and-Illinois alliance, making the Missouri record obsolete.

approvalRequirements: Be a nonresidential customer of a participating Wabash Valley Power Alliance member cooperative at the project location.
Install new qualifying equipment that meets the 2026 PowerMoves technical, efficiency, operational, and customer requirements.
For a prescriptive retrofit, submit the general application, measure worksheet, invoice, specifications, and required documentation within 60 days after installation.
Obtain written preapproval and a funding reservation before purchasing or installing custom measures, and before construction starts for new-construction projects.
Allow pre- or post-installation inspection and satisfy current project caps, completion terms, cooperative submission rules, and available-funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PowerMoves uses defined prescriptive and preapproved custom pathways rather than competitive ranking. A qualifying Indiana member project is likely to receive the rebate after the required documentation and verification, subject to funding; the legacy 23-member title and low-flow-fixture mapping are not current.
reviews.evidenceText: The 2026 PowerMoves business program covers qualifying nonresidential projects for participating cooperative members, with post-installation prescriptive claims and advance approval for custom and new-construction work. Current WVPA materials identify 21 member cooperatives.

approvalRequirements: Be a nonresidential customer of a participating Wabash Valley Power Alliance member cooperative at the project location.
Install new qualifying equipment that meets the 2026 PowerMoves technical, efficiency, operational, and customer requirements.
For a prescriptive retrofit, submit the general application, measure worksheet, invoice, specifications, and required documentation within 60 days after installation.
Obtain written preapproval and a funding reservation before purchasing or installing custom measures, and before construction starts for new-construction projects.
Allow pre- or post-installation inspection and satisfy current project caps, completion terms, cooperative submission rules, and available-funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PowerMoves uses objective prescriptive requirements and a reviewed custom pathway. A qualifying Illinois member project is likely to receive the incentive after proper filing and verification, subject to funding; the legacy 23-member title, old 2023 PDF, and low-flow-fixture mapping require correction.
reviews.evidenceText: The current 2026 business booklet covers qualifying nonresidential Illinois cooperative-member projects and requires timely prescriptive documentation or preapproval for custom and new-construction work. Current WVPA materials identify 21 member cooperatives.

approvalRequirements: Be a residential member of a participating Wabash Valley Power Alliance cooperative at the installation address.
Purchase and install new equipment currently eligible under the 2026 residential program and meet its equipment, sizing, efficiency, configuration, and installer requirements.
Submit the applicable rebate form with the invoice, AHRI certificate, load calculation, product records, and other measure-specific documentation.
File within the applicable current deadline, generally within 60 days of installation.
Allow installation verification or inspection and apply while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential program publishes prescriptive heat-pump, geothermal, thermostat, and water-heating rebates. A qualifying documented member claim is likely to be paid after routine review, subject to available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: PowerMoves currently offers residential cooperative-member rebates for qualifying air-source and dual-fuel heat pumps, geothermal systems, heat-pump water heaters, and Wi-Fi thermostats, with measure-specific documentation and filing requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be a Wakefield Municipal Gas and Light Department residential customer at the installation address.
Use an existing residence and purchase or install a new product or measure currently listed on WMG.L.D.'s residential rebate page.
Meet all measure-specific equipment, efficiency, contractor, permit, replacement, and installation requirements.
Obtain any required preapproval or program enrollment before purchase or work begins.
Submit the applicable form with invoices, receipts, product labels, technical records, and other required proof and permit verification or inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: WMG.L.D. maintains a broad current menu of prescriptive residential incentives and measure-specific forms. A conforming application is likely to be approved, but several legacy mappings, including windows, exterior doors, batteries, and commercial equipment, were not verified on the current residential menu.
reviews.evidenceText: The current residential page lists rebates for appliances, smart thermostats, weatherization, heat pumps, EV chargers, solar, and other selected measures, generally for new products in existing construction and subject to measure-specific applications.

approvalRequirements: Be a WMG.L.D. customer in good standing and own the proposed solar photovoltaic system.
Meet the current system-size, orientation, shading, equipment, contractor, code, and interconnection requirements.
Submit the solar rebate and interconnection package with a stamped one-line diagram, equipment specifications, proof of ownership, contractor agreement, shade report, and other required documents.
Receive full written program and interconnection approval before starting installation.
Complete the approved system, pass inspection and permission-to-operate review, and submit final invoices and closeout records while rebate funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The solar rebate is first-come but uses objective technical, ownership, interconnection, and documentation criteria. A compliant project that secures written approval before work is likely to receive the rebate after final verification; the supplied window-film mapping is unrelated to this solar program.
reviews.evidenceText: WMG.L.D. requires a complete solar and interconnection package and full approval before installation, followed by inspection, permission to operate, invoices, and final review. Funding is first-come and subject to availability.

approvalRequirements: Own an existing Georgia home receiving electric service from Walton EMC.
Propose an eligible energy improvement and use a contractor that meets the HomePlus program requirements.
Apply through Go Energy Financial before work begins and provide the requested borrower, property, contractor, scope, and cost information.
Pass individual credit, income, payment-history, and other lender underwriting requirements.
Do not authorize work until both the borrower and contractor have been approved and the financing documents are complete.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: HomePlus provides a defined financing path, but approval depends on borrower-specific credit underwriting and contractor and project review. An eligible efficiency project alone does not assure a loan.
reviews.evidenceText: Walton EMC directs eligible existing-home customers to Go Energy Financial for HomePlus loans. The current process requires application before work, borrower credit approval, an approved contractor, and project eligibility.

approvalRequirements: Receive Walton EMC electric service at the installation address.
Purchase and install a current qualifying water-heating, heat-pump conversion, geothermal, or waste-heat-recovery measure.
For a fossil-fuel-to-heat-pump conversion, meet the current all-electric system and equipment specifications; dual-fuel systems are not eligible under that pathway.
Submit the current rebate request with the required account, equipment, installation, efficiency, and paid-invoice documentation.
Allow Walton EMC to verify the service location, equipment, and completed installation before issuing the benefit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Walton EMC's current rebates are prescriptive and use objective customer, equipment, conversion, and documentation rules. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be approved after utility verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Walton EMC currently lists rebates for qualifying heat-pump water heaters, fossil-fuel-to-all-electric heat-pump conversions, geothermal systems, electric water heating, and waste-heat-recovery equipment.

approvalRequirements: Be a Waseca Utilities residential electric customer at the installation address.
Select a measure currently listed in the 2026 residential rebate menu and use the applicable measure-specific form.
Meet the current product, efficiency, installation, purchase-date, and customer requirements for that measure.
Submit the form with the invoice, model information, certification, installation records, and other requested documents.
Permit utility review or verification and apply within the current program period while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Waseca's current municipal-utility page provides a 2026 residential rebate menu and measure-specific forms, so a qualifying complete claim is likely to be approved. Exact requirements for every legacy mapped technology could not be verified because several current forms are hosted in externally linked files.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Waseca member page links 2026 residential rebates for ENERGY STAR products, EV chargers, cooling equipment, tune-ups, pumps, fan motors, and aerosol sealing, but the full form text for all mapped measures was not accessible.

approvalRequirements: The project must already be within Washington's first NEVI procurement process because the application period closed on January 31, 2025.

Be an eligible Washington-registered applicant with a site on the identified alternative-fuel corridor segment and meet federal and state DC fast-charging, public-access, uptime, networking, disadvantaged-community, and site-control requirements.
Have received a sufficiently high competitive evaluation and a proposed award.
Negotiate the final scope, budget, match, milestones, and terms and execute a WSDOT grant agreement before relying on funding.
Complete procurement, construction, activation, operations, reporting, verification, and reimbursement requirements under the signed agreement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current application period is closed and WSDOT has already announced proposed Round 1 awards, so a newly identified project cannot enter the round. Existing proposed awardees still require negotiation and signed grant agreements; the mapped vehicle-purchase category is not a NEVI infrastructure use.
reviews.evidenceText: WSDOT reports that the competitive Round 1 application period closed January 31, 2025 and proposed awards were made to five companies for charging sites. Proposed awards remain contingent on negotiation and executed grant agreements.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible commercial, industrial, agricultural, or qualifying multifamily property in a Washington county that has established a C-PACER program.
Propose a qualifying permanent energy, renewable-energy, water, or resilience improvement under the local program rules.
Submit the local program application and the required property, project, technical, savings or public-benefit, cost, and contractor documentation.
Secure private capital and pass the capital provider's underwriting and project review.
Obtain written consent from every mortgage holder or other required lienholder and execute the assessment agreement and lien documents before financing closes.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Washington law authorizes C-PACER, but financing depends on a participating county, local program approval, private-capital underwriting, and written lienholder consent. A qualifying storage project may proceed, but approval is property- and lender-specific.
reviews.evidenceText: Washington's C-PACER statute authorizes locally administered financing for qualifying permanent improvements, including resilience measures, and requires private financing, local review, and written mortgage-holder consent before the assessment lien is established.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an active eligible Washington Gas nonresidential natural-gas account in Virginia.
Install a currently listed qualifying natural-gas measure or propose an eligible custom project with documented gas savings.
Submit the required service-provider, equipment, scope, cost, savings, account, and technical documentation.
Receive written program preapproval before removing or altering existing equipment, purchasing equipment, or beginning installation.
Complete the approved project and submit final invoices, installation records, and any requested inspection or savings-verification documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Virginia business program uses published measures and a defined custom path. Once mandatory advance approval is obtained, a compliant completed project is likely to receive the incentive after verification, although several broad legacy mappings exceed the current specific natural-gas measures.
reviews.evidenceText: Washington Gas currently requires preapproval for Virginia business projects before equipment commitment or installation and then requires qualifying natural-gas equipment or documented custom savings, final invoices, and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Washington Gas residential customer in Virginia at the installation address.
Install a new measure currently offered for Virginia homes and meet the applicable AFUE, ENERGY STAR, AHRI, dual-fuel, replacement, product, and installation specifications.
Use the required participating contractor for heating equipment and satisfy the specific gas-furnace and air-conditioning replacement conditions for any dual-fuel heat-pump incentive.
Submit the contractor or customer rebate claim with the paid invoice, model, efficiency, product, and installation documentation within the current filing period.
Permit program review or verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current Virginia residential rebates are prescriptive and use objective customer, product, contractor, and documentation criteria. A qualifying claim is likely to be paid, but the legacy generic heat-pump and insulation mappings are broader than the current dual-fuel and product-specific offers.
reviews.evidenceText: Washington Gas currently lists Virginia rebates for qualifying furnaces, boilers, a specific dual-fuel heat-pump configuration, smart thermostats, windows, storm windows, and cellular window treatments. Current insulation support was not verified.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Washington Gas residential customer in Maryland at the installation address.
Purchase and install new natural-gas equipment currently listed for Maryland homes and meet the applicable ENERGY STAR, AFUE, AHRI, permit, and replacement requirements.
Use a participating contractor for measures that require the contractor-submission pathway.
Have the contractor submit the current claim, generally within the stated post-installation period, with the invoice, model, efficiency, permit, and installation records.
Allow Washington Gas or its administrator to validate the account, equipment, and completed installation before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Maryland home-heating rebates use objective customer, equipment, contractor, permit, and documentation rules. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid, but the legacy insulation and automated-demand-response mappings are not supported by the current menu, and the prior Smart Energy Rewards offering ended.
reviews.evidenceText: Washington Gas currently offers Maryland home rebates for specified new natural-gas equipment through participating contractors and requires technical qualifications, permits, invoices, and timely claims. The Smart Energy Rewards demand-response offer ended March 31, 2026.

approvalRequirements: Be a Waverly Utilities residential electric customer at the installation address and satisfy the current account or payment-history requirements.
Purchase, install, or retire a measure currently listed in the 2026 residential rebate program during the eligible program year.
Meet the current equipment, efficiency, replacement, installation, metering, new-construction, or recycling conditions for the selected measure.
Submit the applicable rebate form with the invoice, model and efficiency records, installation documentation, or appliance-disposal proof.
Allow utility inspection or verification and apply while annual program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Waverly's 2026 rebates are prescriptive and generally likely after a qualifying customer submits complete documentation. The legacy record overstates several categories: current refrigerator and clothes-washer support is framed as recycling, and envelope support is limited to specific new-home spray-foam and air-sealing work.
reviews.evidenceText: Waverly's current 2026 materials list central air conditioning, air-source and geothermal heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, selected new-home air sealing, appliance recycling, and EV-charger incentives with forms, current-year timing, records, and possible inspection.
